title: Ringed total category for a semisimplicial diagram
statement:
Let $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$ have the finite nonempty ordinals $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and the injective order-preserving maps. Use small sites, sheaves and the size convention [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], [def-weil-size-convention], module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $(\mathcal C_n)$ be a coherent diagram of sites indexed by $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}^{\mathrm{op}}$, with base-change functors and total site as in [lem-trf-slice-site-total-pseudofunctor], [lem-trf-slice-site-total-systems]. An injection $\alpha:[m]\hookrightarrow[n]$ induces $f_\alpha:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_n)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_m)$. Give sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal O_n$ and coherent ring maps $f_\alpha^{-1}\mathcal O_m\to\mathcal O_n$. These determine a ring sheaf $\mathcal O$ on the total site. Its module category $\mathscr M$ is the category of systems $F_n\in\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_n)$ with semilinear transitions, equivalently maps $f_\alpha^*F_m\to F_n$, compatible with identity and composition, where $f_\alpha^*F=\mathcal O_n\otimes_{f_\alpha^{-1}\mathcal O_m}f_\alpha^{-1}F$.
The evaluations $e_n:\mathscr M\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_n)$ are exact and jointly conservative; their derived functors are termwise evaluation. Every $B\in D(\mathscr M)$ therefore has a compatible system $(B_n,Lf_\alpha^*B_m\to B_n)$. Call $B$ cartesian if all these derived transitions are isomorphisms. If every $f_\alpha^*$ is exact, being cartesian is equivalent to every cohomology system $H^q(B)$ having invertible underived transitions. For any coherent augmentation $a_n:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_n),\mathcal O_n)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),R)$ there is a ringed total augmentation $a$; module pullback has components $a_n^*$, and $(La^*E)_n\simeq La_n^*E$ with the canonical composition comparisons.

source.place: Tags 09WC (lemma-simplicial-site-site), 09WF (lemma-describe-sheaves-simplicial-site-site), 0D72 (lemma-restriction-module-to-components-site) and 0D70 (lemma-augmentation-site): ringed, injective-order-map versions of the total construction; the semisimplicial adaptation is agent-supplied.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-slice-site-total-pseudofunctor] and [lem-trf-slice-site-total-systems] to $I=\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}^{\mathrm{op}}$. This is small: its objects are natural numbers and each Hom set is finite. The assumed morphisms of sites supply the extra geometric-morphism hypothesis of the systems equivalence. The equivalence preserves finite products: limits of set sheaves are sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise], and finite products of systems are componentwise because every $f_\alpha^{-1}$ preserves finite products. Consequently the given ring operations and structural ring maps assemble to a ring object $\mathcal O$. A module structure is an abelian-group structure and an action $\mathcal O\times F\to F$ satisfying equations. Under the equivalence these are precisely component module structures with semilinear transitions: compatibility of the action is $t_\alpha(rx)=c_\alpha(r)t_\alpha(x)$. By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], a semilinear map extends uniquely to an $\mathcal O_n$-linear map $\mathcal O_n\otimes_{f_\alpha^{-1}\mathcal O_m}f_\alpha^{-1}F_m\to F_n$, by $r\otimes x\mapsto r t_\alpha(x)$; the inverse sends $x$ to the image of $1\otimes x$. Thus this gives the asserted module equivalence, including morphisms, identities and composition.

source.place: Tags 09WC, 09WF and 0D72, lemma-simplicial-site-site, lemma-describe-sheaves-simplicial-site-site and lemma-restriction-module-to-components-site; face-only adaptation

proof.text: For the fibre inclusion $j_n:\mathcal C_n\to\mathcal C_{\mathrm{tot}}$, a vertical covering and its pullbacks inside the fibre are the same covering and pullbacks in the total site. Indeed an endomorphism of $[n]$ in $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$ is the identity, so the fibre products of vertical maps computed in the fibre have the total universal property as well, by the arrow formula in [lem-trf-slice-site-total-pseudofunctor]. All generating covers of an object $(n,U)$ are vertical, which also gives cocontinuity. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-ringed-restriction] constructs a ringed-topos map $g_n$ with $g_n^{-1}\mathcal O=\mathcal O_n$ and identity structural map; its module inverse image is restriction $e_n$. Kernels restrict sectionwise. Cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; restriction commutes with this sheafification by [lem-pur-native-ringed-restriction-sheafification]. Hence $e_n$ preserves kernels and cokernels, and is exact by [lem-sfb-kernel-cokernel-finite-exactness]. If a module map has invertible components, their inverses commute with each transition by multiplying its commutative square by the component inverses; they therefore form its inverse. The $e_n$ are jointly conservative. No exactness of the semilinear pullback $f_\alpha^*$ has been used. The additive module sheafification used here exists by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] and is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact]; on these small sites its underlying set sheafification is identified by [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets]. Apply [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] to the sheafification unit: its associated-sheaf map is invertible by the universal property, so it is locally bijective. This supplies the restriction lemma’s criterion.

source.place: Tag 09WG, lemma-restriction-to-components-site, proof of (1); Tag 0D72, lemma-restriction-module-to-components-site; continuous/cocontinuous restriction

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], exact $e_n$ induces a functor on the unbounded derived categories, computed termwise on every complex, which is both its left and its right derived functor. Moreover [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $H^q(e_nK)=e_nH^q(K)$, naturally and compatibly with cycles and their quotient maps. These facts hold for unbounded complexes and require neither injectivity of evaluated resolutions nor exactness of $f_\alpha^*$.

Represent $B$ by a complex $K$ of total modules. Choose a quasi-isomorphism $P\to K$ with $P$ K-flat with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the small ringed total site. Each $P_n=g_n^*P$ is K-flat with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], applied to the ringed morphism $g_n$ constructed in step 2. Exact evaluation gives $P_n\simeq B_n$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] identifies $Lf_\alpha^*B_m$ with $f_\alpha^*P_m$. Localize the actual transition chain map $f_\alpha^*P_m\to P_n$ to obtain the asserted derived transition. Naturality of the resolution comparisons in the cited derived-pullback node makes this construction natural in $B$ and independent of the resolution. For composable $[l]\xrightarrow{\beta}[m]\xrightarrow{\alpha}[n]$, pullback preserves flat-term K-flat complexes, so both iterated derived pullback and composite derived pullback are computed on $P_l$. The canonical comparison $L(f_\beta f_\alpha)^*\cong Lf_\alpha^*Lf_\beta^*$ is the one of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], transported along the coherent geometric isomorphism $f_{\alpha\beta}\cong f_\beta f_\alpha$, which commutes with the structural ring maps; by that node it is computed on flat-term K-flat complexes by ordinary module pullback composition, here the tensor reassociation and inverse-image compositor $r\otimes(s\otimes x)\mapsto r c_\alpha(s)\otimes x$. The two transition composites agree by the chain-level system cocycle. Identities follow from $1\otimes x\mapsto x$, and for three arrows both reassociations multiply the three scalar factors in the same order. This establishes the canonical composition comparisons and all required coherence; it does not assert that arbitrary compatible derived systems lift to total complexes.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 0G7E, 06YY and 0D6D: lemma-K-flat-resolution, lemma-pullback-K-flat, lemma-derived-base-change and lemma-derived-pullback-composition; representative proof

proof.text: Define cartesianness by invertibility of the transitions just constructed. Suppose every $f_\alpha^*$ is exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], $Lf_\alpha^*$ is then computed on every complex, so the derived transition is the localization of $f_\alpha^*K_m\to K_n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] its $q$-th cohomology map identifies with the transition $f_\alpha^*H^q(K_m)\to H^q(K_n)$ of $H^q(K)$; compatibility with cycles and quotients in that node fixes this identification on maps as well as objects. If all these maps are isomorphisms, the chain transition is a quasi-isomorphism and hence becomes invertible in the localization. Conversely an invertible derived transition induces invertible maps under every cohomology functor. This proves both directions, in all integer degrees, using the definition of quasi-isomorphism and localization in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 015F and definition-derived-category, Tag 05RU; exact-pullback cohomology criterion

proof.text: For an augmentation define $A^{-1}G=(a_n^{-1}G)_n$, with transition $f_\alpha^{-1}a_m^{-1}G\cong a_n^{-1}G$. The specified augmentation coherence supplies the system cocycle. This functor preserves finite limits componentwise. It has a right adjoint: for a system $F$, take the equalizer of the two maps $\prod_n a_{n,*}F_n\rightrightarrows\prod_{\alpha:[m]\hookrightarrow[n]}a_{n,*}F_n$, where the first uses projection to $n$ and the second uses projection to $m$ followed by $a_{m,*}F_m\to a_{m,*}f_{\alpha,*}F_n\cong a_{n,*}F_n$. The latter arrow is the transpose of $f_\alpha^{-1}F_m\to F_n$. These products and the equalizer exist by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise], since the objects and arrows of the index are small. A map from $G$ into this equalizer is precisely a family $G\to a_{n,*}F_n$ whose adjoint family $a_n^{-1}G\to F_n$ commutes with transitions; [lem-trf-slice-site-total-systems] identifies it with a map $A^{-1}G\to F$. Thus $A^{-1}$ is the inverse image of a geometric morphism $a$. The compatible ring maps $a_n^{-1}R\to\mathcal O_n$ assemble, by step 1, into $a^{-1}R\to\mathcal O$, giving a ringed total augmentation.

source.place: Tag 0D70, lemma-augmentation-site, compatible-family inverse image construction; use all-arrow equalizer for the face-only index

proof.text: Module pullback for this ringed morphism is $a^*E=\mathcal O\otimes_{a^{-1}R}a^{-1}E$. Restriction commutes with the sectionwise presheaf tensor, since it just selects the objects of a fibre; it commutes with its sheafification by [lem-pur-native-ringed-restriction-sheafification]. Thus [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives $e_na^*E=\mathcal O_n\otimes_{a_n^{-1}R}a_n^{-1}E=a_n^*E$, naturally in $E$. Under this identification the transition for $\alpha$ is the ordinary composition isomorphism $f_\alpha^*a_m^*E\cong a_n^*E$: on tensors it sends $r\otimes(s\otimes x)$ to $r c_\alpha(s)\otimes x$, using the coherent identification $f_\alpha^{-1}a_m^{-1}\cong a_n^{-1}$. Its inverse inserts $1$ in the middle factor. Balancing and the coherent structural ring maps make the two maps inverse. The identity and threefold composition equations follow from unit and associative multiplication, with the given inverse-image compositors inserted.

source.place: Tag 0D70, lemma-augmentation-site, and Tag 0D72, lemma-restriction-module-to-components-site; ringed scalar extension

proof.text: For $E\in D(R)$ choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $Q$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], $a^*Q$ represents $La^*E$, and $a_n^*Q$ represents $La_n^*E$. Since evaluation is termwise, step 7 gives $(La^*E)_n\simeq a_n^*Q\simeq La_n^*E$. The complex $a^*Q$ and each $a_n^*Q$ are K-flat with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat]. Hence the derived transition out of the $m$-th component is represented on these very complexes by $f_\alpha^*a_m^*Q\to a_n^*Q$ of step 7. By [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], the canonical comparison $La_n^*\cong L(a_mf_\alpha)^*\cong Lf_\alpha^*La_m^*$, transported along the coherent isomorphism $a_mf_\alpha\cong a_n$ (which commutes with the structural ring maps), is represented on the flat-term K-flat complex $Q$ by ordinary module pullback composition; hence the displayed scalar formula is exactly that canonical composition comparison on these K-flat representatives; its identity and composition equations were verified there. Naturality and resolution independence follow from the resolution comparisons in the cited derived-pullback node. This proves the augmentation assertion with its specified comparisons, without assuming that $a_n^*$ or $f_\alpha^*$ is exact.
